On Sun, Apr 5, 2015 at 5:28 PM, Eric Roth <eroth@intljet.com <mailto:eroth@intljet.com>  wrote: 
Jeffrey, 
I have spent the last couple of hours today reviewing the BBJ, our numerous discussions as well 
as your most recent floor plan request that is very similar to the BBJ featured on Little Bennet. 
When I take into account all of the design and engineering requirements to modify the floor 
plan and refurbish all of the soft goods, cabinetry and metal plating, I believe that when all is said and done, the 
"realistic cost" will run between $4.3M - $5.1M, leaning towards the higher of the spread. 
The down time which is subject to final design, engineering, work scope approval, etc. is 
"realistically" estimated between 9 — 12 months. 
In my opinion, we should fly to Geneva and look at this aircraft together to identify the many 
details that may not be visually present in the photo's you have provided. I also believe that you in particular would 
benefit greatly by physically being in the aircraft and gaining a "spatial appreciation", one that photo's simply can not 
provide. 
Additionally, should you elect to move forward with the pre-purchase inspection, I strongly 
advise that I have an acoustical engineer conduct an acoustical mapping of the complete interior at numerous positions 
within the interior to identify the baseline dBSIL levels. I suggest this take place on the flight from Geneva to Lufthansa 
Technik to take advantage of what presumably will be the sellers cost to move the aircraft. 
As always, don't hesitate to call me with any questions you may have. 
Eric 
ERIC H. ROTH I PRESIDENT

Each exchange related to the TRA is valued using a multi -step process desc=ibed below 
The TRA is valued as 85% of DTA that is created as a result of an AOG excha=ge. The DTA is calculated as: 
cimage002.png> 
The tax rate is the combined federal and state rates. Currently 38.83% for=AGM 
The DTA is then amortized over 15 years. 85% of the tax benefit derived fr=m the amortization for any given year is paid 
out to the individuals that =xchanged. 
Each actual TRA payment then creates additional DTA/TRA calculated as 
TRA payment X the current tax rate 
Notes: 
*The % of the business allocated to taxable entities is calculated as 
the present value of the future cash flows attributable to taxable entities=as a % of the present value of the total cash 
flows of the business. This=% is -75% as of 12/31/2015. 
The key inputs used to determine the present value of the cash flows attrib=table to AMH and the total business are 
o Management Fees and Carried Interest cash flows sourced from the most r=cently approved 5-year Budget Plan 
o Management Fee Cash Flows are discounted by - 8-14% and Carried Interest=Cash Flows are discounted by 20% 
o For perpetual funds and unidentified future funds a Long-Term Growth ra=e of 3% is applied with a discount rate of 
10-20% to determine the Termina= Value of these entities. 
The results of the fair values of the Management Fees and Carried Interest =ash flows are mapped to the appropriate 
parts of the business to determine=the final allocation of value that is attributable to taxable entities.

Chris

Requests the pleasure of your company 
Tuesday, December 14th, 2010 
From 6:30 to 8:30pm 
for a cocktail and an intimate conversation on 
"CONSCIENCE" 
with PROFESSOR YVES AGID 
Professor in Neurology and Biology at the Pitie-Salpetriere hospital, University of Paris 
Co-Founder of the ICM - The Brain and Spine Institute 
Between 5 and 6h Avenue 
RSVP 
or 
About Professor Yves Agid 
With over 600 publications under his belt, Yves Agid, Professor in neurology and biology at the 
Pitio-Salpetriere hospital, University of Paris, is one of the most cited scientists of the past 20 
years. Among his seminal works is the description of various neurodegenerative disorders and 
their associated biochemical and anatomical features, in particular Parkinson's and Alzheimer's 
disease. 
Pr. Yves Agid is a co-founder and the Scientific Strategy Consultant of the "Institut du Cerveau 
et de la Moelle opiniere — ICM (Brain and Spine Institute), an international brain and spinal 
cord research center which is being launched in Paris. With 600 international researchers, 
engineers and technicians and 22,000 square meters of laboratory space, ICM is an innovative 
and ambitious model of excellence in the field of neuroscience.

I don't see how his elaborate efforts go beyond what had been done long before, using primitive technology: 
recording. It gets a lot of data, but doesn't tell us much. 
The particular topic that seems to interest him — what's called "motherese" in the literature (the way parents 
talk to children) — has been studied pretty carefully, notably by Lila Gleitman, the best psycholinguist in the modern 
period, I think (and an old friend). There doesn't seem to be much to it. And it's known that children develop language 
normally under all sorts of circumstances, including conditions very much unlike the ultra-nurturing ones that Roy is 
investigation. E.g., with no input, as in the cases I mentioned. 
And the results about words can't be right. At peak periods of language growth, children are picking them up at 
rate of about one per waking hour. 
Noam

Online Cryptography class: week 4 
Dear Jeffrey epstein, 
The week 4 lectures and problem set are now posted on the course web site at 
https://crypto.stanford.edu/OnlineCrypto 
The problem set is due in three weeks. 
> 
This week's topic is authenticated encryption: encryption methods that ensure both confidentiality and integrity. We will 
also discuss a few odds and ends such as how to search on encrypted data. This is our last week studying symmetric 
encryption. Next week we start with key management and public-key cryptography. 
As usual there is also an extra credit programming project. This week's project involves a bit of networking to 
experiment with a chosen ciphertext attack on a toy web site. 
Enjoy, 
Dan
